newsitem.title: USA: Orange County prosecutors end bankruptcy probe.
newsitem.headline: Orange County prosecutors end bankruptcy probe.

text.p: The Orange County, Calif., district attorney said Thursday's settlement with Merrill Lynch & Co marked the end of its 2-1/2-year investigation into the county's bankruptcy debacle.
"There will be no criminal charges against Merrill Lynch or anyone else," District Attorney Michael Capizzi told reporters at a Santa Ana news conference.
Under the terms of the out-of-court settlement, Merrill Lynch agreed to a $27 million payment to Orange County and to reimburse the $3 million cost of the district attorney's investigation.

The district attorney said the settlement also requires Merrill Lynch to establish a "procedure where all material information about a municipal note issuer is to be gathered, coordinated and disclosed by a designated Disclosure Agent within Merrill Lynch."
Capizzi faced repeated questions from local reporters who wanted to know why Merrill Lynch would not face charges.
